newsitem.title: UK: United Biscuits says recovery on track.
newsitem.headline: United Biscuits says recovery on track.

text.p: British biscuits and snacks group United Biscuits (Holdings) Plc on Thursday announced a return to profit in the first half as its recovery plans started to show results.

Pre-tax profits before exceptional charges in the 28 weeks to July 13 rose to 44.9 million pounds ($69.83 million) from 22.9 million. Profit after exceptional costs was 42.8 million pounds against a loss last time of 37.8 million.
A charge of 60.7 million pounds in last year's first half was set aside to cover losses on the sale of businesses.
Sales fell to 1.05 billion pounds from 1.55 billion, reflecting the company's consolidation efforts.
The dividend was maintained at 3.5 pence a share.
UB has been striving to restore profit growth by getting out of loss-making operations in the United States and Spain and concentrate instead on businesses in Europe and Asia.
Chairman Colin Short said, "We are well into the second phase of our recovery programme, one of underpinning and consolidating the main strengths of UB." ($1=.6430 Pound)
